what_it_does: Density Functional Theory (DFT) is a physics simulation used by chemists and materials scientists to model how electrons behave in molecules; one variant called linear-response time-dependent DFT (LR-TDDFT) is especially expensive because it repeatedly shuffles large amounts of data between a main CPU and helper chips (GPUs, FPGAs). Most of the time is spent moving that data back and forth, not actually doing the math. NDFT tackles this by pushing the computation as close as possible to where the data already lives — a concept called near-data processing, where small processors sit inside or very near the memory chips themselves — so far less raw data needs to travel across the system. The paper shows how to split the calculation intelligently so each type of processor handles the parts it is best suited for, and reports reduced data movement and lower latency.
